hypotheses: H1: Second-line activity is driven by lineage-specific target dependence; e.g., MCF7 for azelaic-acid/MF-101 (ER+/AR pathways), PC3 for lenvatinib (VEGFR/FGFR), HELA/HT29 for hydroxyurea (proliferation).

H2: Second-line activity is dominated by shared systematic response and vehicle-norm threshold effects, so line choice adds little beyond first-line transfer; any line may yield one active/one inactive by chance.
evidence_gaps: No measured second-line responses yet; target annotations are not causal (S3, S4).
Tissue-specific target dependence is not established here (S4).
Activity is a vehicle-norm threshold, not viability; two labels do not establish mechanism (S5).
Source choice and shared systematic response may inflate apparent transfer (S1, S2).
